summary: The NBER working paper audits identical trips on Uber and Lyft and documents price dispersion across platforms. summary: This academic audit analyzes 1.5 million Uber trips from 258 UK drivers before and after dynamic pricing. The authors find that pay decreased, Uber’s cut increased, job allocation and pay became less predictable, and inequality between drivers increased, while explaining how DSAR data can support algorithmic audits of platform work.
